- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices after sharp downward spikes (sentiment < 0.1) — add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag in early periods (first 5–7 days) — adjust upward by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- Overshoots after strong upward moves (sentiment > 0.4) — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak observed in 7-day window.
- When sentiment is flat or negative (0.0–0.2), forecast should be conservative — reduce by 3–6% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is > 10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment — dampen by 1–3% if sentiment is volatile or recent.
